chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He should have two men bear witness when he divorces and when he reverts (to her). If he is ignorant (of the need for witnesses), so he copulates with her, let him keep witnesses now upon what he has done, and she is his wife. So if he had not kept witnesses when he divorced her, his divorce is nothing.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce and remarriage if witnesses were not present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the procedural integrity of 'raj'a' (unilateral revocation of divorce) by requiring two just witnesses for both the initial declaration and the reversion. It highlights a key Shia juristic principle: the validity of the reversion is contingent upon the proper witnessing of the divorce itself, ensuring that the marital bond is legally recognized before it can be restored without a new contract.
